Let me tell you what is really going on out there, folks. On Saturday, March 28, Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan stood up in Palakkad and strongly refuted allegations of a Rs 700 crore corruption linked to the Cooperative Department’s proposed common software project, claiming these serious accusations are merely "politically" motivated. 

This is the exact failure of left-wing governance we see time and again—dodging accountability, undermining traditional public duty, and treating basic integrity like a joke. Instead of upholding order, respecting the rule of law, and answering for the public trust, these leaders just cry foul and duck personal responsibility. When the bedrock of honest governance and social order is threatened, we don't need excuses; we need leaders who respect authority and actually answer for their actions.
